findings.title: $__range guard now checks the interpolated expression and can be silently bypassed
findings.body: querySupportsSplitting() is documented (lines 285-286) as refusing to split queries containing `$__range`, because `$__range` must be resolved on the backend against the split time range. This change interpolates templates at the start of runSplitQuery (line 299), so the guard on line 287 now tests the already-interpolated expression. If template replacement resolves `$__range` (it does when request.scopedVars carries `__range`), the token is gone, isQueryWithRangeVariable() returns false, and queries like `count_over_time({a="b"}[$__range])` get split into chunks. Their results then no longer match what the guard was meant to protect. No test in the diff covers a `$__range` query, so this regression would not be caught. The guard should check the pre-interpolation expression, and the comment at lines 285-286 needs updating since its premise no longer holds.

findings.title: Shard sub-requests are interpolated a second time (and the test locks this in)
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() (shardQuerySplitting.ts line 52) already applies applyTemplateVariables to each target. splitQueriesByStreamShard() then passes every shard sub-request to runSplitQuery() (shardQuerySplitting.ts line 163), and this line interpolates those targets again. The updated shard test asserts applyTemplateVariables is called 5 times (1 for the original target plus 4 sub-requests), which confirms the double application, and the assertion makes it look intended. Template replacement is not idempotent: a substituted value containing a `$name` token gets expanded on the second pass. Ad hoc filters are also passed on every pass, and the shard path now forwards request.filters, which it did not do before. The interpolation should happen at one point, or sub-requests should bypass it through an option.

findings.title: Empty-expression check runs before interpolation, so variables that resolve to empty still execute
findings.body: The `.filter((query) => query.expr)` runs on the raw expression, but the emptiness that matters is the one after interpolation, which this PR now introduces. A query whose expr is a variable resolving to an empty string (e.g. `$query` with an empty value) passes the filter, is classified by isLogsQuery('') as a metric query, and is sent to the backend with an empty expression. The same ordering exists in shardQuerySplitting.ts lines 50-52. Moving the empty-expr filter after the map in both places would make the check match the interpolated value the PR is meant to use.

findings.title: New test only checks the runQuery arguments, not the splitting decisions the change is meant to fix
findings.body: The new 'Interpolates queries before execution' test only asserts that the expr and step passed to runQuery are interpolated. It does not exercise what interpolating first changes: the isLogsQuery partitioning, querySupportsSplitting (including the $__range guard), and the step/resolution grouping computed by calculateStep. There is no case where a variable expands into a logs query, a step variable drives grouping, or a $__range query stays unsplit. Those are the behaviors the PR is supposed to fix, and they are untested.
